name: @projexlight/sdk-sequence
summary: Multi-touch cadence orchestration engine (P14·E1). Defines tenant-scoped outreach/nurture sequences as an ordered list of channel steps (email/sms/call/linkedin/task/wait), enrolls L4 subject personas idempotently by manual call or by event trigger (form_submit/reply/stage_change), and advances due sends through a durable step-executor tick loop that is send-window gated and dedupe-guarded. Adds reactive control (pause-on-reply, stop-on-optout/payment, resume, replace-CTA) and a guard engine (per-subject frequency caps, content dedup, and a per-(tenant,channel) circuit breaker) with an append-only decision audit log. Re-homed from the projex_crm outreach_* tables, normalized (the steps JSONB blob becomes a first-class step table) and re-keyed from user/org scoping to tenant_id + persona identity.

endpoints.description: Create a tenant-scoped cadence definition (name, type, owner persona, default flag); returns 201 with the new sequence.
List all sequences for a tenant (tenant_id query param required).
Fetch one sequence by id within the caller's tenant; 404 when it does not exist.
Create a reusable channel message template (subject/body/variables) that steps reference by template_id.
Append an ordered step (channel, action, delay/schedule, optional template) to a sequence; unique per (sequence, step_number).
Attach an event-based enrollment rule (form_submit/reply/stage_change enter|exit) to a sequence.
Enroll a subject persona into a sequence idempotently; 201 on a new run, 200 when the persona was already enrolled.
Run one durable step-executor tick that claims due execution steps (send-window gated, idempotent next-step enqueue); scheduler/cron-driven, also runs on a timer when SEQUENCE_EXECUTOR_ENABLED.
Apply reactive control to an enrollment: pause, resume, stop, or replace_cta, with reason/event capture and queued-step cancellation.
Evaluate frequency-cap and circuit-breaker guards for a prospective send; returns an allow/block decision and logs it to the guard audit trail.
Record a channel send outcome (success/failure) to drive the per-(tenant,channel) circuit breaker state.
List the append-only guard decision audit log for a tenant, optionally filtered by allow|block decision and limit.

models.description: Reusable channel message body (parity: outreach_templates) with subject, body, variables and channel; referenced by steps via template_id, UNIQUE per (tenant_id, name).
The cadence definition (parity: outreach_sequences): tenant-scoped, typed (lead/customer/onboarding/nurture/custom), status draft|active|paused|archived, at most one default per (tenant, type).

Normalized ordered step definition (was outreach_sequences.steps JSONB): one row per touch with channel, action, schedule_mode/delay_seconds and optional template, UNIQUE per (sequence_id, step_number).

Runtime execution state (parity: sequence_execution_steps): one scheduled touch per enrolled subject_persona_id grouped by enrollment_id, polled by the tick loop on (status, next_run_at), dedupe-keyed for idempotent enqueue.

Event-based enrollment rule (parity: stage_sequence_triggers, generalized): fires on form_submit/reply/stage_change/manual/booking/tag_added at enter|exit, one rule per (sequence, event, stage, edge).
Per-tenant frequency-cap and breaker configuration (cooldown, max_messages per rolling window, breaker thresholds); a missing row means use the defaults.
Per-(tenant, channel) circuit breaker state (closed -> open -> half_open -> closed) with failure/success counts, opened after too many failures and half-opened after cooldown to probe.
Append-only audit log of every guard decision (allow|block with reason: cooldown/max_messages/duplicate/circuit_open), keyed by tenant and subject_persona_id with a content dedupe_hash.

scenarios.title: Define a nurture sequence and add ordered steps
scenarios.when_to_use: When setting up a new multi-touch cadence: create the sequence definition, then append the ordered touches (an email now, a follow-up email after a delay) that enrolled subjects will run through.
scenarios.expected_outcome: A sequence.sequence row is created and two sequence.step rows are attached (step_number 1 and 2, unique per sequence); the second step is scheduled three days after the first when enrollments run.

scenarios.title: Enroll a subject persona idempotently
scenarios.when_to_use: When a contact/lead (resolved to its L4 subject persona) should start a sequence — from a form submit, a manual add, or an event trigger — without double-enrolling a persona that is already running.
scenarios.expected_outcome: On a first enrollment the subject's execution_step rows are queued and already_enrolled is false (the route returns 201); a repeat call returns already_enrolled true and enqueues nothing (the route returns 200).

scenarios.title: Advance due sends with the executor tick
scenarios.when_to_use: When driving the scheduler on demand (or verifying it in a test) rather than waiting for the SEQUENCE_EXECUTOR_ENABLED timer — process the batch of execution steps whose next_run_at is due.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Up to batch_size due execution steps are claimed (send-window gated), each eligible touch is sent and its next step enqueued idempotently; the returned TickResult reports how many were claimed, sent, skipped and deferred.

scenarios.title: Check frequency guards before a channel send
scenarios.when_to_use: When a send handler must respect per-subject cooldown / max-messages caps, content dedup, and the per-channel circuit breaker before actually dispatching a message.
scenarios.expected_outcome: checkFrequencyGuards returns an allow/block decision (with a reason when blocked) and appends a sequence.guard_log row; recordChannelOutcome updates the per-(tenant,channel) circuit_breaker so repeated failures eventually open it.

compliance_posture.notes: Drives outbound outreach across email/SMS/call/LinkedIn, so consent and opt-out obligations apply (GDPR/ePrivacy, CAN-SPAM, TCPA). Reactive control provides stop-on-optout that cancels queued steps, and the guard engine enforces per-subject frequency caps plus a per-channel circuit breaker to prevent over-messaging; every allow/block decision is written to an append-only guard_log audit trail. All rows are tenant-scoped and keyed on L4 subject_persona_id (no direct PII stored beyond the persona reference), so subject-erasure and export requests resolve through the identity spine.
